findings.summary: GoalInterruptBridge._decision_chain fetches decision bodies with bus.messages(WORK_NOTES, limit=board_page_limit) and never passes after_seq. BusClient pages ascending from seq 0 (its docstring: 'on a long-lived channel the plain call returns the oldest messages'), so on a board past 200 messages the decision that answers a suspended question is never in the fetched page: chain is empty, run_once records 'no_decision' every cycle, and the line is never resumed. The production resume path -- spec Goal plus required behaviors 3, 7 and 8 -- does not work on a real board. Tests and the acceptance script miss it because FakeBus holds one or two messages.

DecisionBridge._question_texts has the same ascending-page window (bus.messages(READ_CHANNEL, limit=board_page_limit), no after_seq) and additionally caches the map in self._question_texts_cache for the whole process lifetime. The bounded legacy-owner fallback therefore only ever sees the oldest 200 work-notes messages and never a question note posted after start-up, so _legacy_resolve degrades to legacy_owner_ambiguous and a real legacy parked owner without a persisted question id is still never recovered -- the same outcome the attempt-1 blocker on required behavior 6 named, now from a paging cause rather than a wiring one.

The spec-required legacy-owner-fallback evidence proves only a pure function. scenario_legacy_owner_fallback calls legacy_owner_fallback twice and asserts two outcome strings -- no store, no bridge, no receipt, no resume -- and tests/test_goal_interrupt.py:336-381 does the same. No test or script anywhere passes question_texts to resolve_decision or drives DecisionBridge over a legacy owner, so the newly wired path (_legacy_resolve -> legacy_owner_resolution intent/receipt -> LineOwnerSource.resume) is entirely unverified. The spec's Test requirements demand real bridge process behavior and the receipt ledger, state that handler-only mocks are insufficient, and require proving 'unique legacy owner fallback resumes only that owner; ambiguity performs no resume and leaves fallback active'; none of those three claims is asserted, which is why the paging defect above went undetected.

A suspended line never reaches finalise, so no terminal.json is written for that generation and scheduler park_state (daemon.py:619-628), which requires terminal=='blocked' and waiting_on=='decision', can never see it. ignition.decide therefore re-launches the line process on every cooldown for the whole suspension; each relaunch re-enters decision_interrupt and re-suspends (no coordinator round, no charge, generation preserved since account_last_run sees no new run_id), so spec item 2 holds, but the relaunched line process and the bridge's resume_goal_line can hold the same thread's SqliteSaver checkpoint concurrently.

Two verification facts recorded rather than asserted. This reviewer has file inspection only and no shell, so the prescribed `git diff --exit-code 2731df9a abb063e7 -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` was not executed and tree equality between the two SHAs is unverified; the .dev-dispatch/ namespace as inspected contains only metadata (spec, handoffs, reviews, feedback index), consistent with a compliant metadata-only materialization, and no product file carries review-stage content. Separately, the committed implement handoff records work_head_commit 5fc65acd7ebeb631e3b32e05ffd9a7099fe0a955 while the dispatch context names 2731df9a2954a22c9548cc0dc77bbdfbaee86c2f as the product commit.
